title: Analytical Geometry
summary: Distance, midpoint and gradient; the equation of a straight line in different forms; parallel and perpendicular lines; and the angle of inclination of a line.

notes.latex: d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2} \qquad M\left(\frac{x_1 + x_2}{2}; \frac{y_1 + y_2}{2}\right) \qquad m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}
notes.caption: Distance, midpoint and gradient

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: Find the equation of the line through $A(2; -1)$ with gradient $3$.

items: **Perpendicular** lines have gradients whose product is $-1$: $m_1 \times m_2 = -1$.
Three points $A$, $B$, $C$ are **collinear** (on one line) if $m_{AB} = m_{BC}$.

notes.title: Worked example 2
notes.problem: Find the equation of the line through $P(-2; 5)$ perpendicular to $y = \frac{1}{2}x + 4$.

notes.text: The **angle of inclination** $\theta$ of a line is the angle the line makes with the **positive $x$-axis**, measured anticlockwise ($0^\circ \leq \theta < 180^\circ$).

notes.title: Worked example 3
notes.problem: Find the angle of inclination of the line through $(1; 2)$ and $(4; -4)$.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: If the gradient is negative, the calculator gives a negative angle. Add $180^\circ$ to get the angle of inclination.

notes.title: Worked example 4: angle between two lines
notes.problem: Lines $AB$ and $CD$ have angles of inclination $35^\circ$ and $110^\circ$. Find the acute angle between them.
steps: The exterior angle of the triangle formed with the $x$-axis: $110^\circ - 35^\circ = 75^\circ$.
